title: Redwood Console - Tracing & Debugging Walkthrough
meeting_header: Date: 2026-03-28 | Time: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 62m | Attendees: Samira Khan (Redwood), Jon Park (Redwood), Maria Lopez (Acme), Devon Chen (Acme), Priya Nair (Acme), Liam O'Connor (Acme)
summary: Walkthrough of Redwood Console tracing, error analysis, and request logs focused on debugging flows for a production LLM deployment. Customer asked about retention, SSO/Audit, and ability to tie traces back to request tokens. Discussed hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs and demoed live trace drilldowns and request log filtering. Agreed next steps: send pricing/pilot SOW, share security whitepaper and SOC2 artifact link, run an ingest of 24h of sample logs into a sandbox for benchmark.
transcript:
[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Samira from Redwood, I'm gonna kick us off — joining me is Jon who will do the deep dive. Uh, Maria, Devon — great to have you.
[00:14] Maria: Hi Samira, thanks, we, yeah excited, we had a quick look at the docs, but mostly here to see the tracing and how we'd diagnose errors in prod.
[00:22] Jon: Cool, I'll show the Console traces and request logs, then we can jump into error analysis. Quick note — we'll be using a demo org with synthetic traffic so names and tokens are faked.
[00:34] Devon: Sounds good. Quick context: we're running a mix of hosted endpoints now and some on-prem for PII flows. Our main ask is being able to correlate request->token->model variant, and see per-token latencies.
[00:49] Jon: Yep, that's exactly the type of flow the Console tracing is built for.
[00:55] Samira: Before Jon, Maria can you share timeline? you mentioned Q2 pilot earlier?
[01:03] Maria: Ideally start a pilot in mid April, run two-week perf tests, decision by May. Security review is a hard blocker for us, Priya will lead that.
[01:13] Priya: yes SSO/SAML + SOC2 and audit logs are must-haves, also key management (KMS/HSM) for private deployments.
[01:21] Samira: Totally. We'll include the SOC2 packet and KMS integration notes in the follow up.
[01:27] Jon: Jumping into the Console — (screen share) — this is the tracing tab. At the top you can search by request id, by model, by tenant id, or use time ranges. The spans are auto-grouped; you can expand to see per-stage timings: routing, decode, KV cache lookup, kernel exec.
[01:52] Devon: That KV cache lookup name looks slightly off in the trace, is that the same as KV-cache in our docs?
[01:59] Jon: Yeah sometimes nomenclature in the telemetry can be a little noisy — our telemetry agent reports span names from the runtime and occasionally short forms slip through, we can map them in the UI.
[02:10] [02:10] Samira: (laugh) transcription note: the auto transcription might say 'KV cat' or something — it's imperfect.
[02:18] Jon: Drilling into a slow request — you can see the root cause flagged here: long kernel execution on GPU due to long sequence length. The trace shows token-level timings; you can jump to the request logs to see the prompt and the exact model variant used.
[02:36] Maria: Can you show how we'd alert on regressions? We need to avoid silent quality degradations during rollout.
[02:44] Jon: Sure. There's a QA/Regression panel — you can attach prompt sets and evals; the Console can detect distributional shifts on embedding distances and flag regressions. You can also wire it to Slack or webhooks.
[02:59] [03:05] Priya: On audit logs, can we see who triggered deployments? Our compliance needs traceability.
[03:13] Jon: Yep, audit trails include user id, action type, and request id. Retention is configurable; for Private you can set longer retention and ship to your SIEM.
[03:22] Devon: We have multi-tenant routing rules — can the tracing show which routing policy selected a particular variant?
[03:31] Jon: Yes, the trace metadata includes routing decision and fallback reason. If it fell back due to capacity, that will be annotated.
[03:38] Maria: How about request logs — can you filter by error codes and by token ranges?
[03:45] Jon: You can. (demonstrates) here's filter: status:error AND model:ggml-7b OR token_count:>1024. It returns the requests and you can open the raw payload, masked according to your data retention/PII settings.
[04:02] Liam: Masking is key for us. Does Redwood do automated PII masking or do we provide scrubbing rules?
[04:10] Samira: We support both — automatic heuristics and custom redaction rules that run at the edge. For Private deployments you can plug in your own scrubbing pipeline.
[04:20] Jon: Now showing error analysis workflow — we cluster similar errors and surface probable root causes. For example, "truncate_failure" in this demo was due to premature tokenization mismatch. You can click a cluster to see representative traces and the top affected endpoints.
[04:39] Maria: That clustering looks useful. Is it possible to export the cluster data for our SRE playbooks?
[04:46] Jon: Absolutely — CSV or JSON exports, and you can link back to the original request ids for replay in a sandbox. We also have a notion of a 'trace snapshot' that captures the minimal state to reproduce the issue.
[04:58] Devon: Replays — can we replay against a pinned model version in Dedicated?
[05:04] Jon: Yes, you can replay in a sandbox pinned to a model binary/quantization profile; replay tooling supports workload-level rate limiting so you don't flood prod.
[05:15] [05:20] Priya: For the SOC2 reviewers, do you provide attestations for log integrity — e.g., append-only storage or hash chaining?
[05:29] Jon: We provide tamper-evidence options; for Private we can integrate with your HSM for signing logs, or we can ship log digests to an external witness. We'll add the architecture note in the security packet.
[05:41] Maria: A quick question on cost: you talked before about token-level billing and caching — how do traces help reduce unit cost?
[05:50] Samira: Good one. Traces let you identify high-latency, high-token paths (e.g., long prompt prefixes) — with Optimize recommendations you can change batching, enable prefix-KV caching, or pick a cheaper model variant for non-critical requests. That gives measurable token savings.
[06:07] Jon: Showing a sample trace of a reranking flow — you can see the pre-rerank embeddings call and the main generation, and the Console shows aggregate token counts per route.
[06:20] Liam: For our PII flow we need guaranteed delete of logs after 30 days — is retention policy per-tenant?
[06:27] Jon: Yes retention is per-tenant and per-log-type. For hosted we'd enforce the retention in our pipeline; for Private you control the retention directly.
[06:36] Maria: Ok demo was great. Could you also show how we would onboard — sampling, bandwidth, and a small benchmark?
[06:44] Samira: Sure — our typical pilot is 2 weeks: we run a 24–72h ingest of production-like traffic into a sandbox, run the tracing and error analysis, then do a performance benchmark. We'll provide a pilot SOW and a pricing outline.
[06:58] Devon: Can Jon run a quick example of searching request logs for a particular request id and showing the linked trace?
[07:04] Jon: Yep, searching now — paste request id 'rq_20260328_7b9a' — there it is, trace opens and you can see the span where the fallback occurred. The UI highlights the fallback reason and suggests a mitigation: increase dedicated capacity or change routing policy.
[07:22] Priya: For the legal folks, can you surface the exact retention window for request logs in the contract?
[07:29] Samira: We'll include explicit retention settings and SLAs in the SOW.
[07:33] Maria: One more — how does tracing work across hybrid deployments; e.g., a request routed from hosted to Dedicated?
[07:42] Jon: Traces propagate with a global trace id; when it hops between deployments we annotate the hop and include the region and host. We also support cross-cluster KV cache correlation.
[07:54] Maria: Nice. Any limits on trace volume or ingestion cost?
[08:00] Samira: There are ingest tiers; for pilots we include a small ingest quota. For production we bill based on trace volume and retention tier; we'll share the pricing doc.
[08:09] [08:15] Devon: Could you share a link to the benchmarking spreadsheet you referenced?
[08:18] Samira: Yup, I'll include the benchmark sheet and the Console walkthrough recording.
[08:22] Jon: Also will drop the security whitepaper and SOC2 artifacts link.
[08:26] Maria: Great.
[08:28] Samira: Ok quick recap and next steps.
[08:31] Jon: Recap — showed trace drilldowns, request log filters, error clustering, replays, and audit capabilities.
[08:38] Maria: That covered our main concerns.
[08:41] Samira: Next steps: we'll send pricing and SOW, security pack, and a sandbox link for sample log ingestion. When can we expect sample logs?
[08:49] Devon: We'll try to get a 24h sample by next Friday.
[08:52] Samira: Perfect. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links.
[08:57] Maria: Thanks, bye.
[09:00] [call ends]
